original_question: Is every orderable abelian-by-nilpotent group an O* group?
target_in_paper: Section 3 (Totally ordered groups), Open Problem 3.20*: "Is every orderable abelian-by-nilpotent group an O*-group?"
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper’s target almost verbatim. It has the correct ambient object (groups), the correct hypothesis class (orderable abelian-by-nilpotent groups), and the correct property being asked about (being an O*-group). It also stays on the exact open problem rather than drifting to nearby questions such as Engel orderable groups, nilpotent-by-abelian embeddability, or groups with nilpotent commutator subgroup.
missing_details: The paper’s notation O*-group should be spelled out: a group G is an O*-group if every partial order on G can be extended to a total order on G making G a totally ordered group.
To make the question stand-alone, say explicitly what abelian-by-nilpotent means: there exists a normal abelian subgroup A ◁ G such that G/A is nilpotent.
Make the universal quantifier explicit: the question ranges over all groups G with these properties.
It helps to spell out that "orderable" is being used in the Section 3 sense of admitting a total order making G a totally ordered group.
There are no finiteness, rank, presentation, or additional nilpotent-by-abelian assumptions in Problem 3.20, so a stand-alone rewrite should avoid suggesting any such extra hypotheses.
Use the paper’s exact hyphenation/notation O*-group rather than "O* group."
refined_question: Let G be a group admitting a total order that makes G a totally ordered group, and suppose that G has a normal abelian subgroup A such that G/A is nilpotent. Must every partial order on G extend to a total order on G making G a totally ordered group; equivalently in the paper’s notation, must every orderable abelian-by-nilpotent group be an O*-group?
justification: This is exactly the open problem stated as Problem 3.20* in Section 3 of the paper (p. 16). The only essential context missing from the draft is the definition of O*-group, given in the "Further notation" paragraph at the start of Section 3 (p. 15), and the need to unpack abelian-by-nilpotent so the question is self-contained. I did not broaden the problem to neighboring questions, because Comment 3.20 (pp. 18-19) distinguishes nearby classes: orderable metabelian groups are already known to be O*-groups, certain abelian-by-nilpotent R*-groups that are also nilpotent-by-abelian are known to be O*-groups, while orderable groups with nilpotent commutator subgroup need not be O*-groups.
